hotspots.title: 1. PC Case
hotspots.description:
A PC case directs airflow across high-heat components to optimize cooling. It provides structural support to prevent heavy components from sagging and uses standoffs to prevent electrical short circuits. Cases also protect hardware from dust, liquid, and static, dampen fan noise, safely enclose spinning parts, and provide front-panel ports and internal cable routing.

This 3D model is based on the Corsair 4000D ATX Case.

hotspots.title: 2. PSU
hotspots.description:
Power Supply Unit (PSU)

The PSU converts mains AC power into low-voltage DC power required by internal components. It: Supplies power to the motherboard, CPU, storage and peripherals Includes voltage regulation and protection features Unstable or poor-quality power supplies can damage hardware, cause unexpected shutdowns and increase the likelihood of data loss.

This 3D model is based on the Corsair MR850x PSU.

hotspots.title: 3. GPU
hotspots.description:
Graphical Processing Unit (GPU)

A specialised processor designed to perform many calculations simultaneously, making it ideal for rendering graphics, processing video, and now, AI. The GPU frees the CPU to focus on general-purpose processing and enables smooth performance in applications like games, 3D modelling, and virtual reality.

This 3D model is based on the nVidia GEFORCE RTX 3080ti GPU.

hotspots.title: 4. Storage devices
hotspots.description:
Storage devices provide long-term, non-volatile data storage. Common types include:

  • Hard Disk Drives (HDDs) – magnetic storage with moving parts.
  • Solid State Drives (SSDs) – faster, more durable semiconductor storage.
  • M.2 Drives – ultra-compact, high-speed SSDs that connect directly to the motherboard.
  • Removable media (USB drives, external disks).
Storage devices often contain sensitive operating system files, credentials, logs and user data. If not encrypted or securely managed, they present a significant security risk.

This 3D model is based on the Samsung 970 Evo M.2 SSD 2TB.

hotspots.title: 5. RAM
hotspots.description:
Random Access Memory (RAM)

RAM is the computer’s short-term working memory. It: Temporarily stores data and programs currently in use Allows the CPU to access information quickly Is volatile, meaning its contents are lost when power is removed Insufficient RAM can slow system performance and increase system errors, while faulty RAM can cause crashes that disrupt secure operations.

This 3D model is based on Trident RGB RAM.

hotspots.title: 6. CPU
hotspots.description:
Central Processing Unit (CPU)

The CPU is the “brain” of the computer. It: Interprets and executes instructions from software and the operating system Performs calculations and logical operations Coordinates the activity of other hardware components Modern CPUs are installed into a socket on the motherboard and rely on cooling systems (heatsinks and fans) to prevent overheating. Poor cooling or sustained overheating can cause system instability and hardware failure — which can indirectly increase cyber security risk through crashes or data corruption.

This 3D model is based on the intel I7-9700k CPU.

hotspots.title: 7. Motherboard
hotspots.description:
The motherboard is the backbone of the computer. It: Connects all internal components using electrical pathways (buses) Hosts the CPU, RAM, chipset, storage connectors and expansion slots Contains firmware such as BIOS or UEFI that starts the system A compromised or misconfigured motherboard firmware can undermine all other security controls.

This 3D model is based on the ASUS ROG STRIX Z370-E motherboard.

scene.title: Router Anatomy
scene.description:
Explore the Cisco C8500-12X router in 3D.

More details...

The Cisco Catalyst C8500-12X is a high-performance enterprise edge router designed to provide secure WAN connectivity, SD-WAN, cloud networking, and advanced routing services for medium to large organisations.

It features twelve 1/10 Gigabit Ethernet (SFP+) ports and delivers high-throughput performance for services such as VPN, encryption, firewalling, and traffic segmentation.

scene.title: Sim Network
scene.description: Build and test a network — tutorial practice map, then office level. Maps are listed in layouts-index.json stages.

config.scene-help-content:
You are an IT network technician. The company "eNetworks" is setting up a new office and you are tasked with bringing internet connectivity to all devices.

In this immersive scenario, place devices, connect cables, and check your networking skills with the Test Connection button.

  1. Use the left palette to place network devices on the grid.
  2. Use Cable mode to connect devices along the floor.
  3. Press Test to check connectivity from the Comms Cupboard.
  4. If the test fails, press Try again and keep troubleshooting.
  5. Click on cells that contain devices and cables for more information and options.
